55452292.title: File:A Medieval decorated square floor tile, part of a four-tile pattern (13th – 14th century). - - - (FindID 190437).jpg

ObjectName.value: A Medieval decorated square floor tile, part of a four-tile pattern (13th – 14th century).

Categories.value: Portable Antiquities Scheme|Images uploaded by Fæ|Portable Antiquities Scheme, LON|Tiles in the Portable Antiquities Scheme

Artist.value: Museum of London, Kate Sumnall, 2007-10-05 11:20:47

ImageDescription.value:
A Medieval decorated square floor tile (13th – 14th century). This tile is one from a four tile pattern. One edge is missing from the tile; the front surface is decorated with a two-tone pattern. One corner is blocked out with white clay creating a curved edge for the internal design, within this white clay a single red lozenge-shape is visible. Much of this corner is obscured so the white clay may just form a circular band. The internal circular field is decorated with two circular floral motifs with an annulet above and a red cross within a white pentagram below. The two circular motifs are identical but on is white on red and the other is red on white. They comprise and six-petalled flower with central pellet all enclosed within two concentric circles. On the reverse and the unbroken sides are the remains of white mortar for attachment.

Similar but not identical patterns are illustrated in Eames (1980: nos3013, 3060, 3070)

Dimensions: length: 109.07mm; width: 87.36mm; thickness: 23.50mm; weight: 360g.

Reference: Eames, E. 1980. Catalogue of Medieval Lead-Glazed Earthenware Tiles. Volumes 1 and 2. British Museum Press: London.

14397128.title: File:St Andrew's church - medieval floor tiles - geograph.org.uk - 1634092.jpg

ObjectName.value: St Andrew's church - medieval floor tiles - geograph.org.uk - 1634092

Categories.value: Taken with Canon PowerShot S3 IS|Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland|Medieval European tiles|Information field template with formatting|Images by Evelyn Simak|Floor tiles in England|Encaustic tiles in the United Kingdom|14th-century encaustic tiles|St Andrew's, Barton Bendish (interior)|Church tiles in Norfolk, England

ImageDescription.value: St Andrew's church - medieval floor tiles. St Andrew's > 1634049 - 1634070 is the only one of three churches in the village which is still in use. St Mary's church > 1634138 - a couple of hundred metres further to the west - became redundant in 1976 and is now in the care of the Churches Conservation Trust. No traces remain of All Saints church > 1634114 which was situated across the road from St Andrew's. Tower and chancel of St Andrew's church were built in the 14th century, whereas the inner doorway > 1634066 dates from around 1200 and shows a merging of Norman and Gothic styles. The porch > 1634065 with its elaborate flushwork, depicting saltire crosses, was added in the 15th century. The church was restored in the 19th century and the stained glass windows > 1634080 date from that time. There are 17th century box pews on the north wall, one of them with the date 1623 carved into the door > 1634089. The simple octagonal baptismal font is C15 > 1634108. Of particular interest is the chancel > 1634076 floor in that it has retained the complete set of original 4 inch square medieval tiles, decorated with varying patterns. And even rarer still is the 14th century piscina > 1634098 with a double drain in the floor below it, which was probably in use during the 13th century when the ritual called for piscinae with two drains. There is no other known example of this combination of two drains in the floor and one in the wall.
